citations.quote: Assume AC. In dimension $d\ge4$, a one-handle whose feet lie in the same connected lower stage can be replaced, by an interior framed circle surgery, with one $(d-2)$-handle. The resulting manifold may change, but its entire boundary, specified collar and every later attaching map are identified with the old ones. The framing for this existence trade is the displayed product framing. Separately, surgery on a prescribed rank-three-framed circle lying in a product three-dimensional level of an oriented four-manifold, with its framing homotopic to a level rank-two framing plus the level-normal line, is represented relative to the unaffected boundary by adjoining two four-dimensional two-handles on that framed knot $K$ and a small disk-framed zero meridian $U$. The statement retains the integral framing of $K$. In a two-handle trace every interior framed circle can be put in this form by the preceding circle lemma. The pair's boundary identification is the boundary-relative local O3 identification.

Assume full AC. Let $N\cong D^2\times S^1$ be an oriented solid torus in the interior of an oriented smooth 3-manifold, let $K$ be its core with any integral framing, and let $U$ be a small meridian of $K$ with the zero framing given by its meridian disk. Simultaneous framed surgery on $K$ and $U$ returns a solid torus diffeomorphic to $N$ by a diffeomorphism equal to the original identification on $\partial N$. Thus inserting or removing this pair preserves the ambient manifold relative to the complement of $N$, including external collars and boundary parametrizations. An embedded colored ribbon graph avoiding $N$ is fixed. No assertion is made that a graph traversing $N$ is fixed, or that this operation belongs to a complete relative move list.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $n$-manifold with collared boundary $\partial W=\partial_0W\sqcup\partial_1W$, let $\varphi:S^{k-1}\times D^{n-k}\to\partial_1W$ be an attaching embedding of a $k$-handle and let $\psi:S^k\times D^{n-k-1}\to\partial_1(W\cup_\varphi h^k)$ be an attaching embedding of a $(k+1)$-handle attached after it, where $0\le k\le n-1$. If the attaching sphere of $h^{k+1}$ meets the belt sphere of $h^k$ transversely in exactly one point, then $W\cup_\varphi h^k\cup_\psi h^{k+1}$ is diffeomorphic to $W$ relative to $\partial_0W$. Consequently a geometrically cancelling consecutive pair may be deleted from, or added to, any handle presentation of the same manifold; the diffeomorphism may be taken to act only in a collar of the affected boundary disc and in the two handles, so the attaching data of all later handles are carried along.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $h_1,h_2$ be $k$-handles attached to $M\subseteq\partial_+W$ as in the slide definition, with $1\le k\le n-2$, and let $h_1'$ be a slide of $h_1$ over $h_2$ (the slid handle attached to $M$ by the band move). Then $W\cup_{f_1}h_1\cup_{f_2}h_2$ and $W\cup_{f_1'}h_1'\cup_{f_2}h_2$ are diffeomorphic relative to $\partial_0W$; more precisely there is a diffeomorphism supported in a neighbourhood of the two handles and the band region carrying the first presentation to the second. Consequently a handle slide does not change the diffeomorphism type of the presented manifold and may be performed on any of two equal-index handles.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $V$ be a compact
smooth $n$-manifold with boundary and let $N$ be a smooth $n$-manifold without
boundary ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $F:V\times I\to N$ be a smooth map such
that $F_t:=F(\cdot,t)$ is a smooth embedding for every $t\in I$
([[def-smooth-embedding]]), and suppose $F$ is constant near the ends: for some
$\varepsilon\in(0,\tfrac12)$ one has $F(x,t)=F(x,0)$ for $t\le\varepsilon$ and
$F(x,t)=F(x,1)$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon$, for all $x\in V$.

Then for every open neighbourhood $W\subseteq N$ of the compact image
$F(V\times I)$ there is a smooth map $H:N\times I\to N$ such that
$H_0=\operatorname{id}_N$, every $H_t$ is a diffeomorphism of $N$
([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]),
$$H_t\circ F_0=F_t\quad\text{for every }t\in I,$$
$H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, $H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$
for $t\le\varepsilon/2$, and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.

citations.quote: Assume AC. Let a finite smooth relative four-dimensional handle movie be based on a compact oriented three-manifold $N$, with its boundary product collar fixed. Let a distinguished one-handle persist from a cancelling $1/2$ birth to a cancelling $1/2$ death, with no one-handle slides involving it on the interval. All feet, actual framed two-handle attaching strips, slide bands, local birth/death supports and outgoing identifications are supplied. Choose a framed replacement arc in $N$ joining its feet and carry it by the foot isotopy; assume other birth/death supports miss its tube. Replacing the one-handle by interior surgery on its core joined to that arc, then cancelling the long two-handle, gives a based framed-link movie. Its changes are framed isotopy, $O2$ band slides (including a meridian slide when a strip crosses the replacement arc), and $O3$ at its two endpoints. Here $O3$ is a framed knot with its small disk-zero meridian. All framings and actual outgoing boundary maps are retained, and the boundary collar is fixed pointwise. The statement permits arbitrary homotopy class of the replacement arc and arbitrary finite signed traversals by the other strips. It is local conversion of the supplied movie, not its global existence.

Assume AC. Fix one four-dimensional one-handle with feet in a connected compact oriented three-dimensional base $N$, and a finite system of actual framed two-handle strips. Let $B,B'$ be any two framed replacement arcs with the same parametrized foot germs and avoiding other feet and the protected boundary collar. The routed link outputs of the continuous one-handle replacement, with their actual outgoing identifications, are connected by finitely many exterior framed isotopies and $O2/O3$ moves, fixing that collar. The core knot in an $O3$ move need not be nullhomotopic. For disjoint arc interiors one comparison consists of adding $K=B'\cup(-B)$ with its small zero meridian $V$, sliding each routed traversal over $K$, sliding $V$ over the negative old zero meridian $U$, and deleting the resulting clean $O3$ pair. All framings, prescribed attaching strips and outgoing maps are retained.

Assume full AC. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional collared bordism, $d\ge1$, and let $f_s$ be a path supplied by [[lem-relative-one-parameter-morse-path-with-finite-events]], with the given noncritical height fixed on the spatial collars. Prescribe descending endpoint fields, stationary near the parameter ends, standard near their Morse critical points, and having no trajectories from index $i$ to index $j\ge i$. Morse–Smale endpoint fields suffice. Then there is a smooth descending family $X_s$ with those endpoint and collar values such that:

1. Near every fold it is the negative Euclidean gradient of the exact cubic model. At every regular critical point it has a smooth hyperbolic descending model. Near each same-index passage it may be taken to have the normalized linear Morse model at the destination.
2. No ordinary trajectory increases index. The entire family has finitely many same-index connecting trajectories; each occurs at a distinct parameter away from births and critical-value crossings. Each is a transverse parameter passage: on an incoming section at its destination, the $i-1$ source-sphere tangent directions together with the parameter direction map isomorphically onto the $i$-dimensional normal space of the stable section.
3. A sufficiently small parameter neighborhood of each birth contains no same-index trajectory. Between its two newborn critical points there is exactly the standard cancelling trajectory.
4. In successive one-critical elementary bands, the full framed attaching embeddings and actual outgoing boundary maps vary smoothly on each regular function chamber, including through positive-index-drop tangencies. The existing elementary birth and critical-value-crossing comparisons retain their actual outgoing maps, and their composition retains the terminal boundary parametrization.

Disconnected $W$, empty ends, and index $0/d$ births are allowed. This is an elementary-band assertion: it neither asserts slice-wise Morse–Smale transversality at positive index drops nor supplies parameterwise grouping of arbitrary based handle presentations by index or a global Kirby completeness theorem.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge4$, and let $V$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional bordism with corners, horizontal faces $A_0,A_1$, and vertical face $B\times[0,1]$, with compatible product collar charts fixed. Here $\partial A_i=B\times\{i\}$. There are excellent Morse data with all critical points interior, equal to the specified height $t$ on a fixed smaller vertical product collar, zero and one on the horizontal faces with their prescribed inward collar models. They give a finite handle decomposition whose attaching thickenings lie in the interiors of horizontal levels, away from the fixed vertical collar, retaining the actual outgoing identification. Critical values may be ordered by index while this entire boundary height is fixed. If $V,A_0,A_1$ are connected and $A_0,A_1$ are nonempty, there is such a relative presentation with no handles of index zero or $d$. No fundamental-group assumption or h-cobordism hypothesis is imposed.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(f,X)$ be adapted on a compact triad, and choose regular $0<u<c<c'<v<1$ such that the critical set in $K=f^{-1}[u,v]$ consists exactly of finite clusters $P,Q$ at values $c,c'$. Suppose there is no $X$-trajectory from a point of $Q$ to a point of $P$. Then for any $a,a'\in(u,v)$, including $a>a'$ or $a=a'$, there is an adapted Morse $g$ with the same critical points and indices as $f$, $g=a$ on $P$, $g=a'$ on $Q$, and $X$ still downward gradient-like for $g$. The function is $f$ outside the interior of $K$ and near its two end levels, and is $f$ plus a constant near every critical point. On a triad with just these two critical clusters, one may also use its face levels as $u,v$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold with boundary admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, let $K\subseteq M$ be compact, and let $W\subseteq M$ be open with $K\subseteq W$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:M\to [0,1]$ that equals $1$ on an open neighbourhood of $K$ and satisfies $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq W$.

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$. For each $p\in M$, let
$\gamma_p:I_p\to M$ be the maximal integral curve through $p$, and set

$$ \mathcal D:=\{(t,p)\in\mathbb R\times M:t\in I_p\}, \qquad \Phi(t,p):=\gamma_p(t). $$

Then $\mathcal D$ is open in $\mathbb R\times M$, each fibre $\mathcal D_p$ is
an interval containing $0$, the map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ is smooth, and
$\Phi$ is the unique maximal local flow generated by $X$.

Assume AC. Let $(F_s,X_s)$ be the weak relative descending family of [[lem-relative-descending-path-with-finite-same-index-passages]] on a compact $d$-dimensional collared bordism. Its vertical product height and endpoint fields are fixed. There is a smooth family $g_s$ with the same critical points, indices and exact positive-affine cubic birth models, such that $X_sg_s<0$ off the critical points and all critical heights are ordered by index. The boundary height is unchanged. The family has finitely many simple same-index critical-value crossings, no triple values or simultaneous two crossings, and no such crossing at a same-index trajectory event or at a fold. The only other coincidences are the intended folds. The trajectories, their finite same-index passages, full framed local data and actual terminal identifications are retained. Positive-index-drop tangencies are allowed.

Assume full AC. On a compact smooth collared bordism, keep the incoming and outgoing parametrizations as part of a finite elementary handle description. A generic adapted function path supplied by [[lem-relative-one-parameter-morse-path-with-finite-events]] induces a finite sequence of changes of its Morse-induced elementary handle descriptions: relative diffeomorphisms and isotopies of the framed attaching embeddings, changes of standard handle-coordinate frame, splitting/merging empty product bands, interchange of two independent disjoint framed attachments, and creation/removal of a geometrically cancelling adjacent-index pair. At every change retain the induced outgoing boundary map and carry every later attaching embedding and final boundary parametrization by it. Changes of descending field within a single elementary band alter its framed attaching embedding and outgoing map only by the corresponding isotopies. The birth cancellation has exactly one connecting trajectory. Disconnected bordisms, empty ends, and index $0/n$ pairs are included.

This is a comparison of parametrized elementary bands with their actual cancellation boundary maps retained. It does not suppress those maps, classify an arbitrary global path of descending fields by slides, or assert surgery/Kirby/coupon completeness.

Assume full AC. Let $q$ be an index-$k$ Morse critical point in dimension $n$, $1\le k\le n-1$, with fixed local coordinates and descending field $f=c-|u|^2+|v|^2$, $X=(2u,-2v)$, for $(u,v)\in\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}$. Let $p$ be a higher critical point of the same index. Suppose a one-parameter family of the descending attaching-sphere sections of $p$ passes through the stable section of $q$ once, at one point, and transversely in the following sense: its $k-1$ sphere-patch directions and its parameter direction map isomorphically onto the $k$ unstable directions at the event. Assume all remaining attaching data are disjoint from the chosen local passage region; retain the joining band, lower regular level, and normal framing, and assume no intervening critical point between that region and the chosen lower level.

The two framed attaching embeddings obtained by transporting below $q$, before and after this isolated passage, differ by the signed framed band sum with a parallel of the attaching sphere of $q$. For $k=1$ this replaces one foot by a parallel of the other foot of $q$ along the band. For $1\le k\le n-2$ this is the handle slide of the existing definition and preserves the relative diffeomorphism type with all later attaching maps carried along. In particular $n=4,k=2$ gives the framed-link slide. For $n=3,k=2$, only the stated local surface band sum with its supplied embedded band is asserted; no higher-codimension band-existence contract is imported. No generic-family existence or global trajectory-completeness assertion is made.

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$. For each $p\in M$, let
$\gamma_p:I_p\to M$ be the maximal integral curve through $p$, and set

$$ \mathcal D:=\{(t,p)\in\mathbb R\times M:t\in I_p\}, \qquad \Phi(t,p):=\gamma_p(t). $$

Then $\mathcal D$ is open in $\mathbb R\times M$, each fibre $\mathcal D_p$ is
an interval containing $0$, the map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ is smooth, and
$\Phi$ is the unique maximal local flow generated by $X$.

Let $k,m,n\ge1$ and $p\in\mathbb N$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+n+p}$ be open, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^k$. Suppose $F(a,b,\lambda_0)=0$ and $D_yF(a,b,\lambda_0)$ is invertible. Then there are neighbourhoods and a unique $C^k$ map $\varphi$ solving $F(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda)=0$. More precisely, on suitable open neighbourhoods $P$ of $(a,\lambda_0)$ and $Q$ of $b$,

$$F(x,y,\lambda)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y=\varphi(x,\lambda),$$

and

$$D\varphi(x,\lambda)=-D_yF(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda)^{-1}D_{(x,\lambda)}F(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda).$$

When no parameter block is present, this is the ordinary $C^k$ implicit function theorem.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $V$ be a compact
smooth $n$-manifold with boundary and let $N$ be a smooth $n$-manifold without
boundary ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $F:V\times I\to N$ be a smooth map such
that $F_t:=F(\cdot,t)$ is a smooth embedding for every $t\in I$
([[def-smooth-embedding]]), and suppose $F$ is constant near the ends: for some
$\varepsilon\in(0,\tfrac12)$ one has $F(x,t)=F(x,0)$ for $t\le\varepsilon$ and
$F(x,t)=F(x,1)$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon$, for all $x\in V$.

Then for every open neighbourhood $W\subseteq N$ of the compact image
$F(V\times I)$ there is a smooth map $H:N\times I\to N$ such that
$H_0=\operatorname{id}_N$, every $H_t$ is a diffeomorphism of $N$
([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]),
$$H_t\circ F_0=F_t\quad\text{for every }t\in I,$$
$H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, $H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$
for $t\le\varepsilon/2$, and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. If the attaching sphere of $h^{k+1}$ meets the belt sphere of $h^k$ transversely in exactly one point, then $W\cup_\varphi h^k\cup_\psi h^{k+1}$ is diffeomorphic to $W$ relative to $\partial_0W$. Consequently a geometrically cancelling consecutive pair may be deleted from, or added to, any handle presentation of the same manifold; the diffeomorphism may be taken to act only in a collar of the affected boundary disc and in the two handles, so the attaching data of all later handles are carried along.

Assume AC. Let a finite smooth relative four-dimensional handle movie be based on a compact oriented three-manifold $N$, with its boundary product collar fixed. Replacing the one-handle by interior surgery on its core joined to that arc, then cancelling the long two-handle, gives a based framed-link movie. The meridian of the $i$th filling solid torus is glued to the surgery-framed parallel $\lambda_i$ on $\partial N(L_i)$.

A decoration is a finite properly embedded oriented framed ribbon graph, with fixed abstract coupon set, actual coupon morphisms and band labels, fixed attachment order, and prescribed product ribbons in $C$ meeting only the designated marked boundary intervals. Colored graph isotopies keep all these collars, endpoints and labels fixed. Then:

2. Two such exterior decorations that are isotopic as framed labeled graphs in $Y_L$ are connected by finitely many exterior framed colored graph isotopies and framed slides of open graph strands over the surgery parallels $\lambda_i$. Original coupons and colors remain fixed.

Suppose the **marked undecorated relative surgery calculus** holds in $Y$: every required collared bordism has a marked surgery presentation, and every specified orientation-preserving identification of two outputs, fixed pointwise on $C$, is realized up to isotopy relative to $C$ by a finite sequence of the canonical local undecorated moves $O1$ (a separated $\pm1$ unknot), $O2$ (a framed surgery-component band slide), $O3$ (a framed knot plus a small zero-framed meridian), and exterior link isotopies. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. citations.quote: Assume AC. Let $N,M$ be connected nonempty compact oriented smooth three-manifolds, with their boundaries identified with the same oriented surface $\Sigma$ in the bordism convention and with fixed compatible product collars. There is a finite framed link in $\operatorname{int}N$ whose surgery is diffeomorphic to $M$ with the prescribed external boundary parametrization. It may be realized as a four-dimensional two-handle trace with those marked horizontal faces and vertical collar $\Sigma\times[0,1]$. More generally this holds componentwise for a specified common component partition; empty input is treated by the empty union. In particular a fixed connected standard base with the required boundary may be chosen on each component, and a closed component may use $N=S^3$. An explicit connected standard base is the complement in $S^3$ of standard handlebodies placed in pairwise disjoint balls, one for each boundary component with its specified genus, with the given surface parametrizations attached to these boundary copies. This is relative surgery existence, not equivalence or completeness of surgery moves. Decorations may be carried by the resulting actual diffeomorphism; a complete decorated move theorem is a separate assertion.

Assume AC. Let $N$ be a connected nonempty compact oriented three-manifold and let $W_0,W_1$ be connected four-dimensional finite two-handle traces from that same fixed base. Their full common boundary $Y$ and all horizontal, external and corner collar identifications are marked. Suppose a connected compact oriented five-bordism $V$ between them is supplied with its full vertical product collar $Y\times I$ fixed. Then finitely many O3 insertions on each original framed link give two descriptions of the same actual four-dimensional two-handle trace $W_*$ from $N$, with the full marked boundary retained. Here each O3 insertion is a framed knot and its small disk-framed zero meridian, with its actual boundary-relative identification. No condition on any fundamental group is required. In conjunction with the projective-plane stabilization supplier, split signed unit-framed unknot insertions first supply such a $V$ whenever needed. This is a common-middle existence assertion; it does not assert that the two descriptions of $W_*$ are related by a complete O2/O3 movie.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge4$, and let $V$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional bordism with corners, horizontal faces $A_0,A_1$, and vertical face $B\times[0,1]$, with compatible product collar charts fixed. Here $\partial A_i=B\times\{i\}$. There are excellent Morse data with all critical points interior, equal to the specified height $t$ on a fixed smaller vertical product collar, zero and one on the horizontal faces with their prescribed inward collar models. They give a finite handle decomposition whose attaching thickenings lie in the interiors of horizontal levels, away from the fixed vertical collar, retaining the actual outgoing identification. Critical values may be ordered by index while this entire boundary height is fixed. If $V,A_0,A_1$ are connected and $A_0,A_1$ are nonempty, there is such a relative presentation with no handles of index zero or $d$. No fundamental-group assumption or h-cobordism hypothesis is imposed.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(W;M_0,M_1)$ be a compact triad and let $f$ be
an adapted Morse function whose critical points of index $k$ all lie at one
level $c\in(0,1)$, with no critical point of another index at $c$ and no other
critical value in a neighbourhood of $c$. Then the
sublevel just above $c$ is obtained from the sublevel just below $c$ by
attaching disjoint $k$-handles, one for each index-$k$ critical point.
Equivalently, handles of equal index attached at one level may be regarded as
attached simultaneously or successively in any order, the result being the same
up to diffeomorphism fixing the incoming face and respecting the lower sublevel up to homotopy of pairs. On the common attached-stage model, reordering disjoint attachments fixes its entire lower stage. Handles of equal index may
be reordered freely, and attaching embeddings may be changed by isotopy of the
attaching region.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $N$ be compact with $\partial N=\partial_-N\sqcup\partial_+N$, and let $f_N:N\to[0,1]$ be Morse, with $f_N^{-1}(1)=\partial_+N$ and $f_N=1-t$ on a critical-point-free outgoing collar. Attach a $k$-handle along an admissible framed embedding $h:S^{k-1}\times D^{n-k}\to\partial_+N$, obtaining $N'$. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ there is a Morse $f':N'\to[0,1]$, equal to $f_N$ on the part of $N$ outside the outgoing collar strip $t<2\varepsilon$ and near $\partial_-N$, whose old critical points and critical values are unchanged and whose only new critical point has index $k$ and value $1-\varepsilon/2$. Its endpoint fibre at one is the new outgoing face, and $f'=1-t'$ on a smaller outgoing collar. Its handle attachment is the prescribed one, up to compatible collar and corner choices.

The height of the whole old outgoing face must be lowered before the new critical band is glued. Pointwise agreement on that face, or identification of every saddle level with a product attaching tube, is not asserted.

Assume full AC. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $n$-manifold, $n\ge1$, with fixed product collars, and let $f_0,f_1:W\to[0,1]$ be excellent adapted Morse functions equal to the same noncritical product height on those collars. There is a smooth path $F_s$ joining them, stationary near its parameter endpoints and fixed on smaller boundary collars, with finitely many exceptional parameters. Each exceptional parameter contains exactly one of: a corank-one interior birth/death with nonzero kernel cubic and nonzero parameter unfolding, or a transverse crossing of two nondegenerate critical values. All other critical points are nondegenerate, all other critical values are distinct, no two events share a parameter, and a birth value differs from every other critical value. The critical locus is a compact smooth curve whose parameter projection has only nondegenerate folds. Each fold creates or destroys two critical points of adjacent indices with distinct critical values. By a homotopy supported near each fold, preserving this event list and the endpoints, the path can further be put near that fold in smooth parameter-dependent spatial coordinates into the form

$$F_s=a(s)+b(s)u+c_0u^3+Q(y),\qquad b(0)=0,\quad b'(0)\ne0,\quad c_0>0,$$

where $Q$ is a fixed nondegenerate quadratic form in $n-1$ variables. Empty ends, disconnected $W$, and index $0/n$ pairs are allowed. This is a function-path statement with fixed product height; it has no boundary critical events and asserts no global descending-field or surgery-move theorem.

Assume full AC. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional collared bordism, $d\ge1$, and let $f_s$ be a path supplied by [[lem-relative-one-parameter-morse-path-with-finite-events]], with the given noncritical height fixed on the spatial collars. Prescribe descending endpoint fields, stationary near the parameter ends, standard near their Morse critical points, and having no trajectories from index $i$ to index $j\ge i$. Morse–Smale endpoint fields suffice. Then there is a smooth descending family $X_s$ with those endpoint and collar values such that:

1. Near every fold it is the negative Euclidean gradient of the exact cubic model. At every regular critical point it has a smooth hyperbolic descending model. Near each same-index passage it may be taken to have the normalized linear Morse model at the destination.
2. No ordinary trajectory increases index. The entire family has finitely many same-index connecting trajectories; each occurs at a distinct parameter away from births and critical-value crossings. Each is a transverse parameter passage: on an incoming section at its destination, the $i-1$ source-sphere tangent directions together with the parameter direction map isomorphically onto the $i$-dimensional normal space of the stable section.
3. A sufficiently small parameter neighborhood of each birth contains no same-index trajectory. Between its two newborn critical points there is exactly the standard cancelling trajectory.
4. In successive one-critical elementary bands, the full framed attaching embeddings and actual outgoing boundary maps vary smoothly on each regular function chamber, including through positive-index-drop tangencies. The existing elementary birth and critical-value-crossing comparisons retain their actual outgoing maps, and their composition retains the terminal boundary parametrization.

Disconnected $W$, empty ends, and index $0/d$ births are allowed. This is an elementary-band assertion: it neither asserts slice-wise Morse–Smale transversality at positive index drops nor supplies parameterwise grouping of arbitrary based handle presentations by index or a global Kirby completeness theorem.

Assume AC. Let $(F_s,X_s)$ be the weak relative descending family of [[lem-relative-descending-path-with-finite-same-index-passages]] on a compact $d$-dimensional collared bordism. Its vertical product height and endpoint fields are fixed. There is a smooth family $g_s$ with the same critical points, indices and exact positive-affine cubic birth models, such that $X_sg_s<0$ off the critical points and all critical heights are ordered by index. The boundary height is unchanged. The family has finitely many simple same-index critical-value crossings, no triple values or simultaneous two crossings, and no such crossing at a same-index trajectory event or at a fold. The only other coincidences are the intended folds. The trajectories, their finite same-index passages, full framed local data and actual terminal identifications are retained. Positive-index-drop tangencies are allowed.

Assume AC. Let $W$ be a compact smooth four-dimensional bordism with fixed horizontal faces, fixed vertical product height, and specified all-two-handle endpoint presentations. Apply the finite weak descending-path supplier and its parametric index grouping, with the endpoint fields prescribed from those presentations. Then there is a finite based framed mixed-handle movie joining the given endpoint presentations. Its elementary changes are framed isotopies, same-index handle slides (index3 read as the reverse index1 slide), cancelling adjacent-index births/deaths and commuting critical-value interchanges of disjoint attachments. Older attachments may pass through a birth block; the finite normalizing slides and actual cancellation maps are retained. Every higher attaching embedding and the complete terminal parametrization are carried by the actual outgoing comparisons. All supports fix the vertical boundary collar. No slicewise Morse–Smale condition at positive index drop is required.

Assume AC. Let $N,M$ be connected nonempty compact oriented smooth three-manifolds with their external boundary parametrizations and vertical product collar fixed. Let $W$ be a connected compact oriented four-bordism between them. Suppose two specified all-two-handle presentations of $W$ are joined by the finite index-grouped based mixed-handle movie of [[lem-index-grouped-relative-descending-paths-give-based-framed-handle-movies]], with its actual terminal maps. Their framed links in $N$ are related by finite exterior framed isotopies and $O2/O3$ moves. The cumulative outgoing map is the comparison prescribed by that marked movie, up to isotopy fixed on the protected collar. Here $O2$ is the specified framed component band slide; $O3$ inserts or deletes an arbitrary framed knot and its small disk-zero meridian. Intermediate four-dimensional traces may change by the displayed interior surgeries. No assumption that diffeomorphic four-dimensional two-handlebodies are two-equivalent is made.
